lines.text: [announcer voice] Welcome one, welcome all, it's DVDASA with your hosts Steve Lee, Bill Poon, and Valentin. Here we go! Here we go! Alright. Alright guys, so I got a special guest calling in. I'm gonna give him a call.
Really hard to get a hold of this guy, but a huge fan of the show. — He called you, or you called him? — I'm gonna call him. — I mean, how did the whole thing...
Go ahead. I mean, he's just been dying to get on. It worked out in his schedule, so here we go. — Can you put it on speakerphone? We'll be all off here. — Yeah.
That's not too loud. I don't think this is as high as it goes. — Where are you going with it? — There you go.

[phone connects] Oh, shit. What's going on? — What's going on? You tell me what's going on. What are you doing? Where are you? — That's Bill. — Who's over there? Who am I talking to? — Bill, this is Pooner.

The four caballeros are here. Bobby. — Am I on speakerphone right now? — Yes. — Bobby, how many fucking times did I tell you: when I call you, why don't you just announce immediately that I'm on speakerphone?

Oh yeah, that's true. — A lot of horrible information got out. A lot of oopsies. I mean, I don't know how many times I've called Bobby. [beat] Can you guys hear the echo? I'm in the shitter right now.

No, you sound clear. — Because, you know, sometimes there's someone in the car, and I don't usually have a lot of small talk when I call Bobby. I just jump right into, like, 'Get this person out of my will,' or 'Fuck this person' — and that person will be sitting right in the car next to him.

It's only happened once. For future reference: when you call me and I'm on speakerphone, the first thing before you say hello or anything is, 'Hey, you're on speakerphone.' And I go, 'Oh, okay, cool.'
So who am I on speakerphone with right now? — You're on speakerphone with Steve, Valentin, Pooner, me, Bob, and Alex. You got all the guys here. So it's a bro show. — Yeah. It's a bro show.

It's a bro show. [the guests we lined up] fell through. Well, fuck them, whatever — the show must go on. I love it when you guys do shows without me, which is never. We were talking about that earlier. I would love it.

Whatever is happening right now, I would love it if you guys did this all the time. For me — almost like an OCD kind of thing — I just want to make sure that there's always a show every Tuesday, every Thursday.

And I'm also super busy right now, and I'm dealing with my shit right now. Speaking of dealing with shit — since this is a self-description joke — I have a health thing I gotta say. — Go ahead. — So basically, Bob, you know my life in L.A.: eating a lot of unhealthy food, a lot of french fries, a lot of greasy fried shit, and not exercising at all. And the obvious answer

from my doctor, or from anybody, is like, 'Hey, once you start exercising and eating healthy, you're gonna feel great.' And you're like, yeah — you just... what does that even mean? What does 'feeling great' mean? And then we've got this continuing joke of, like, girls
don't fart, girls don't shit — and then you have me on the other end of the spectrum, that just shits constantly. So I actually have a huge announcement to make right now.
Basically, I have been eating right — literally juicing and eating salads for like a few weeks — and I don't fart anymore. — No! — Really.

Listen to me, man. I walk around all day and I'm like, something's missing, something's off, like what's going... I can have a full meal, and — you know, old habits die hard, old behavioral patterns and all this kind of shit.

Like, literally right now, if this was the past, my shit would have been done already. But I'm literally just sitting on the toilet, because I'm like, oh — after a huge meal, I usually just go shit right away.

But I literally have one movement a day, and I don't ever fart. Ever. Like, not ever — nothing even close to it. Farting was just part of my life. I would just fart all the time, like every hour on the hour.
Now it's almost surprising. I'm like, 'Oh fuck, I just farted right now.' — You miss it? — I feel fantastic. I feel great, and I never fart anymore, and I barely shit.

And when I shit, it's like I almost need no toilet paper. It's one solid huge log that just shoots out, and I'm wiping, and I'm like, 'Oh, wow.' I literally could have wiped my ass with one tiny square of toilet paper.

So yeah, sometimes out of old habits, I'll just sit on the toilet and I'll be like, 'What am I doing?' I'm sitting there waiting for the shit to come out, and I'm like, oh — I don't shit five, six times a day anymore.

So what's your diet? You're just juicing and salads? — I'm juicing, and yeah, I eat salads. And I don't know — I've sort of secluded myself. I don't want to say where I am, but I've secluded myself in an area where there aren't that many restaurants or that much food, so I almost have no choice, you know?

And I'm really, really working on my ADD, no-attention-span kind of shit, because I feel like that's just the way the world is now. Like kids today with no attention span. I'll listen to the first ten seconds of every song, and listen to like a hundred

songs, and never listen to any of them all the way through. So now I give myself little assignments — listen to one song all the way through, watch one TV show without changing the channel or checking what else is on. So that I'm present, and you have my complete attention for that period of time.
So I will say, though — I fucking miss you guys. — We miss you too, Dave. We miss you too, man. — It looks like you guys are out there still fucking getting your nails done and shit.
It's crazy without you, man. Chaos happens when you're not around. — What? I mean, what's going on with you? — Hey, on that front, I'll have to remind you later.

I can't do the shows on Monday nights and Thursday nights anymore. — Why? What happened? — Well, because I got this gig, this part-time gig — like a private show. I'm cooking for this couple, and they asked me to do it Monday and Thursday nights.

And you got that job specifically through the show? — Yes, directly from you. — Look at that. Look at all these doors opening up for you. — I was thinking about that. I was in their kitchen today and I was like, wow — a lot of the good stuff going through my life right now is coming through the show. — Absolutely.

Right. Well, I think — you know, we talk a lot of shit on the show, and a lot of the comments we get are like, 'Oh yeah, it's the conversations people have in the back, the way you actually talk to your friends but would
never say out loud.' And they go, 'Was Dave ever really gonna buy a soccer team for Steve Lee?' And it's like — it is and it isn't.
You know, if Steve was completely committed to doing that, then I would. I'm feeding off everyone else's energy too. I'm not just in this vacuum by myself.
I know Bobby would like to think I could sit in a room and just podcast by myself for hours and hours — which I actually have done in the past, but... — I'm still down to go to Macau.

I'm down for Macau, dude. I'm telling you right now, I'm down for Macau. I'm at a place right now where I see a therapist maybe three times every two days. So I'm literally — you know what they call them, shrinks.
Like I'm literally getting my brain shrunk. — Oh, wow. — [mock therapist voice] He's like, 'All you do is talk about Steve Lee. You're obsessed with this guy. Okay, David, let's stay on point.'
'Let's go back to what you were saying before.' I know, but this guy Steve — he's like, 'Stop for one second.' I go, 'Let's talk. It's all I think about. It's all I care about.'
So we're going to go to Macau, right? Me and you, buddy. — It's against your therapy. It's not healthy, is it? — The physicians and producers I've been contacting to make sure your album is on point,
the directors I've been contacting to make sure your music video is going to be amazing — this is all... I'm doing this if you want it, you know? If you don't want it, then I don't want to.
Dude, the album is dope. It's a dope album. It's very good, to me it is. Actually, it was kind of... — You know, on the ride over, Steve was telling me he's almost done with all his stuff, right?

Is that what you're saying? — Yeah, I got like eight or nine songs done. — Okay, first of all, that's great, because that's you working on your own shit. Then the next phase is for you to learn those rhymes, say it like a million times. — Oh, I'm nowhere close to that. This is just me

reading it off the paper. — Yeah, so you have to live it. You know, when you see rappers and they just know their songs — — Yeah, I'm not there yet. This isn't rap, but you know — I do fifteen-minute segments for HBO now, I do a lot of voice work, and so

I'm like, oh, that's easy — I go in the studio sound booth and I recite. [mock ominous voice] 'And that's why the end of the world is coming.' Dave, do the little accordions. 'And that's why the end of the world is coming.'

And then I say it a million times until it's just one line, and at some point I don't have to read it off the paper. I can be like, 'The end of the world is coming,' and say it a million different ways until it becomes art.
Right, right. Money Mark, Dan the Automator — as many producers rolling through there and working on this music for you. — Wait, you got the Automator on board? — I got everyone on board. — Oh, wow.
I got everyone on board if you're on board. You're going to have Dan the Automator, Money Mark, and a few other guys that we'll keep under wraps right now.

Wow, dude, that's... — It's all... you know, I don't want to be like a soccer mom and get too excited, because it's like that weird overbearing dad, like, 'I'm living your dream through you' — all that kind of shit.
Well, just between all of us — I've actually quit doing comedy because of the album. I'm focusing so much on the album, because it's hard to write jokes and raps at the same time.
So I've just been so focused. When I'm not at Fat Sal's, literally I'm not even playing video games. I'm making beats and I'm writing, writing, writing. I'm doing this shit.

I'm taking it seriously. It's not like I haven't done anything. I could bring some stuff in for you guys to even listen to. I've really been focused. But I had no idea about the Big Bear thing and all this other stuff going on.

So that's actually good news. I told you in text, but I want to tell you — over the phone right now — I don't know if you've ever been pushed. I know you create in your own way, but I want to push you, and some of it might be uncomfortable.

But I want to push you. You said, 'out of my comfort zone,' that you try everything, right? That you try everything, and you're like, 'This is something I would never do' — which is my life now. I do shit all fucking day that I would never do. Like I would never fucking have a juice
for breakfast, you know? — Right, right. I mean, that's fucking gross. I'd rather have... — You know what? You're absolutely right. To grow as a human, you've got to go out of your comfort zone.

You can't just stay in your little comfort bubble. — Yeah. And you know what? You're already growing. You're saying, 'I'm working on my album instead of playing video games all day.' That's fucking awesome.
Yeah. And that's a choice I decided to make, because when it comes to music, I want it to be good, you know? I don't want to just put out crap.

I want to actually sit down and put energy into it, instead of just... I know on our show we get into a funk sometimes — or I should say I get into a funk sometimes — and then all we do is focus on, like, anal sex, or the orgy, or the orgy,

or... — Well, I mean, we're still going to have an orgy, but... — We'll focus on horrible shit, and all that does is attract the most horrible people and horrible energy. But it's good if we're feeling good. Like, Bill — without knowing how good a chef Bill is, I know that's a motherfucker who loves to cook.
Right. Because, A, he's fat, so that means he loves to eat. And anyone who loves to eat enjoys food, you know? Whether it's shitty food or good food, they definitely enjoy eating.
And because I'm a fan of the Poon Report — before it was the Poon Report, it was YumYumCha — Bill's the original blogger. He takes pictures of food, he writes about food, he talks about it.

So my educated guess is that Bill is probably a really good chef. I mean, there's a difference between a chef at a restaurant and a chef for your friends, but on that level, I think you could definitely make a good meal. And you said to us before,
'Hey, is there a kitchen at the studio? Because I'd like to cook for you guys.' Someone who isn't a good chef would not say that, you know? — Well, they seemed to like it today.
I cooked my first meal for them, and they seemed to like it. So I'll be back there Thursday. — Awesome.

Well, I sort of feel like crying right now, because I feel like you guys are in there doing the Lord's work, and I'm here doing my juicing, not taking imaginary shits. But — I actually hate to be that guy, but I have to go into my therapy session right now, so I have to cut this short.

And I'm super jealous. I wish I was in the studio right now bullshitting with you guys. — When are you coming back? — I'm coming back soon. I'll be there next week. — Oh, awesome. — Yeah, we're gonna get this shit cracking, we're gonna start making some good stuff. — Cool. — I'm just talking about it.
Alright, crew. You guys are awesome. I miss you guys. I'll be home soon. Have a good show. Bro show. — Thanks, Dave. Thanks, Dave. Have a good session yourself. — Thanks. Alright. Bye, guys.
See you soon. Bye, Dave. [call ends] — Wow, that was a nice special guest, man. That was cool. I haven't heard from him for a long time. Seems like he really misses it here. — Oh, yeah.

Yeah. I mean, I'd never seen that side of him, where he got kind of emotional like that. — Well, I remember he used to say that the one thing about the show was that the show was where he got his contact with people.
Because usually, when he's not doing the show, he just does his own thing. But the show — he says he doesn't have friends, and the show is where all his friends are.

Oh, right, right, right. Seems like he's handling his business and actually growing from his experience, wherever he is. — Yeah, you know what? Whenever Dave grows, I'm always worried, actually. — What was that?
I'm always worried. You know how people who eat really bad stuff then become a vegetarian? — Yeah. — And they do it for a long time, and all of a sudden it just changes them too much?

And that's why I'm afraid all of a sudden he'll change too much. — So he's not eating cheeseburgers? — Yeah, not because of the diet, but just in general — whenever he goes through his therapy or whatever, I'm like, is he going to be somebody else?

That's what I'm always afraid of. — Like, where it completely changes him? — Yeah. — I don't think that's going to happen. — I don't know. Because it seems like he was — I don't want to say fighting going — but he seemed like he was voluntarily going.
Right, right. But it seems like he's still kind of in between both worlds. — Yeah, we'll see. So where the hell's Alex? — Yeah, where is he? I was just about to introduce him.
Is he taking a dump? — He's busy. — Alright. So we'll talk about something else, because we're going to talk about — — Yeah. I mean, that's a long thing, though, right?
Yeah. I mean, I could just talk about maybe one aspect. I don't want to — I'm no expert on this stuff. I know you guys mentioned, like, people want to hear more about the reptilian thing.

Okay. Give us a summary. — I'll just give you a brief — I'm going to mention one lady I've been researching. Her name is Peggy Kane. K-A-N-E. And what she does — I don't know where she lives — but she does something called electronic voice phenomenon.
And what that is, is capturing spirit voices on recorders. — She uses just, like, normal — — Oh, really? Normal? — Yeah, just normal recorders. But there's some kind of static, like a filter system.

It's open, where spirit voices can enter — it's like the white noise. — There was a movie out. — Kind of like that, kind of like that. But she's experienced even realer things, where reptilians have entered her world.

Like, see, this is the thing. We're in the third dimension, but she mostly talks about the lower astral dimension, which is closest to our dimension. It's basically the place we all go when we're in sleep, in deep sleep.

They say our spirit goes to this dimension, and it's darker — kind of like Earth, but a darker world, like a predatorial world. — And do you call them reptilian because they look like reptiles? — Yeah, I mean, yeah. There's

different names — like, I'm no expert, again, I'm no expert with this, I just like reading about it and looking stuff up when I'm hella bored. But what happens is, she puts this stuff through, like, a filter in the software.

And she has this technique — because before, when these spirits were contacting her, it'd be, like, some dude from the 1940s who died a long time ago, just kind of messing with her. But then she uses a technique where she does reversals with these programs, this software, where she's able to detect the lies

from these spirits, so she can find the truth of these statements. But dude, if you ever get on YouTube, she has this very disturbing — I don't know exactly where to find it — where she has reptilian... — Like she speaks in tongues?
Yeah, where there's, like, five of them in her living room. — So if you don't have the tape recorder, will you still hear them? — No. That's what enables her to hear these things.

We can't hear them, because — this is the thing — these reptilians live beyond our five senses. — Right, right. — They could shapeshift. They live off human fear. A lot of the satanic rituals are based on that, because that's the whole reason they're here.

They actually have this planet on lockdown. There's, like, a net around it. I know it sounds crazy, but that's the stuff. — Well, I'm just wondering — so if you don't have this tape recorder, you'll never hear them.

So it's kind of out of mind, right? — Yeah, because they obviously shapeshift, they're multidimensional. — So when they shapeshift, do they shift into beings you can then see here on Earth? — You know what, I've heard different stories about this. Basically, a lot of them, they —

the people in power, like politicians — I mean, this could be a conspiracy — but they're actually controlling a lot of it. The bloodline is mixed, like half. Like, you know, they say the Bushes, you know what I mean?
Or the Rockefellers. A lot of it is mixed in with reptilian. It's interbreeding through history. I mean, these things have been here thousands — they've been here a long, long time.
They're highly technologically advanced. — What is this whole thing called? — I don't know, I'm just burning out. — What do you mean? Like, this whole genre. — I don't even know what to call it.

It's not, like, new-agey. It's definitely — if you type in 'conspiracy theories,' it'll probably come up if you type in 'reptilians.' But even if it's just for the story itself, it's interesting stuff.

My newest song that I'm writing is called 'Memories of the Void.' And it's about an experience I had when I was sleeping and then entering that world. Have you guys ever experienced, like, you're in the dream world, and in order to wake up you go through some kind of — like in the Matrix, you know, like

the Matrix has that telephone or something. I have, personally — there's a certain place when I'm ending a dream, like a portal, for us to come back to this dimension. I've experienced that. I don't know about you guys — you might not remember it, that might be suppressed. — Yeah. — Is it
required for us to go through this portal to come back? — I wouldn't be able to answer that, but I know for me personally, I've experienced it a lot of times.
It's like some kind of line, or a dormitory room, that I go into. I go in there, then I can wake up and be in this world. But that's just me personally.

I don't know if you guys have experienced anything like that. I know it sounds crazy, and I sound like a crazy person when I talk about this stuff. But yeah, they say you do enter this lower astral dimension.
It's a predatorial world. Reptilians do exist there. There's actually a lot of pillaging and rape. It's basically like Earth, but a lot darker — a darker world.

But this world is the lower astral plane. When we dream, supposedly that's the world our spirits go to. — But so what — you know what? Going back to that story I told you about, when I listened to Portishead

at ASU — and I saw those dead people — that kind of validated my personal experience. Because seeing that made me question this whole existence and a whole bunch of stuff. It really opened my mind up to other possibilities. I thought,

if you're just a normal human being, you're born, you go to grade school, boom, you go to college, you get married, you have two kids, you retire — normal people just view that as life. But we're basically suppressed. We

should be further than we are as a human race. Like, I should be able to look at you and read your thoughts — telepathy, telekinesis, stuff like that. But these reptilians, they're suppressing us. That's what they're doing — they're

suppressing us and taking our personal power away from us as humans. — So when we go into this lower astral plane through our dreams, are those reptilians looking for us and wanting to kill us in there? What's going on? — No, I don't see that. Then again, I don't

really have a personal experience of it. I've experienced elements of evil and weird things, but I couldn't personally tell you, like, I saw a reptilian at the end of the hallway and I'm running — like the final battle in 'V.'

But I could tell you glimpses of dark stuff, where I end up in — — Because I have some pretty good dreams sometimes, like happy dreams. — Yeah, I mean, I'm not saying this is completely — it's not hell.

But you have to also consider: this dimension, okay, we're in the third, right? This dream one is in between — this is the fourth. So there's one higher, even better than that, the good dreams you're having.
But this one is still kind of a dark world. — Oh, I see. — And, you know, maybe religions describe that world as hell. I don't know.
See, that's — I'm no expert. I'm just telling you the stuff I like to read about. Oh, another one — if you guys want to look up this book: Linda Moulton Howe, 'Glimpses of Other Realities.'

That's the other book that kind of opened my mind. It has crazy stuff — like a chapter where this dude gets shifted into a different world, and he's on some spacecraft, and he sees a clone of himself. There are illustrations. — Yeah? — Get that book for sure. Cop that book, 'Glimpses.'

Have you met anyone who shares the same ideology? — No, not at all. And that's why I feel weird talking about it. It's kind of hard. My brother — when I picked this book up, it was hard to find. First of all, they don't sell it
at Borders. You have to go on the internet to find it. I wasn't home, so I had to go to the post office. My brother picked me up from the post office, and we're in his car.

He's like, 'Dude, what's in the box, man?' I was excited — I'd been waiting for this book, I'd been doing research. I'm like, 'Oh, man, this book.' And then he got scared. He's like, 'What is that book?' He started flipping through it, saw these illustrations of aliens and reptilians and greys and stuff, and he's like —

he got scared. He was like, 'Dude, if you don't stop this, I'm gonna have to send you to a loony bin, an insane asylum.' I thought he was gonna cry. Because it sounds so crazy, all these things. But — I don't know, it makes sense to me.

I think hallucinogenics have a lot to do with it, because it does open your mind to different dimensions and realities. I saw it, man, I'm telling you — I saw a wall filled with people. They were human, and they were there, dude. It wasn't like Tom and Jerry, a cartoon.

It was human beings. Suffering, mourning human beings, like this. They're like, 'Hey, we're here. Do you see me?' That type of thing. And I had Portishead — maybe that first album, 'Dummy,' track three, whatever that song is — on repeat, too. So I don't know, maybe music is that powerful.

So do you think they were trying to get help from you? — They definitely wanted to expose themselves, to let me know they were there and they were suffering. Because that was not the only time I saw those dead people.
My homie got arrested that day, because I ruined his trip — I told you, he ran across campus and got pepper-sprayed. And I ended up going back, smoked a Newport, and laid on my back,
and there — it was that type of texture. See the ceiling, how it is? They covered my whole dorm room ceiling, dude, these people. They were looking down at me.

Different age groups, man. An old lady, a young girl — just everything. — Were they humans that got caught in there, or reptilians trying to warn you? — See, that's the thing. I've been five years sober now, and reflecting back, I think what I saw that day was a portion of the lower astral dimension, where

— because it's the closest to ours — I was enabled to see it for a brief window. Because after that, I didn't even like to think about it. I mean, we had — I had a brief experience, because our house in Poway was, like,

haunted — it was probably built on some Indian burial ground, and I was held down by spirits. But visually I wasn't able to see; that was more audio. — When's the last time you had an experience with lower astral people?
Just in that house in Poway. And my brother, every single family member did too. Both my folks admitted to it. So that's been a while, though. That was in the '90s, dude. That was like '92.

So you haven't experienced it recently, then? — No. It has a lot to do with where you're located. Poway — there's a lot of cowboy, Indian history there, you know what I'm saying? So most likely that house was built on some kind of burial ground, and the people down there weren't content or something. Because on that experience, there was —

I was half asleep, half awake, and I was being held down, and there was, like, whispering — a bunch of different voices — and I'm like, 'Oh, I can't move.' And my brother — that hallway, it was on that side of the house.
He had the same experience. He jumped into the pool to get rid of these demonic — or these, I don't know what they were. So that's what I wrote down. — Are your parents still in that house?
No, we moved. But I asked them in Gilbert. I go, 'Did you know — was it haunted?' Because I told them about my experience. We were at the dinner table, and they both — my dad had a run

from the garage to their master bedroom sometimes, because he was so scared. And then my cousin Eddie — I told him that story, and he told me the same thing. He's like, 'Dude, there's something about that house, man.'
Did you ever look into it? Maybe there was a murder or something that happened there? — No. The street was Ranch — it's called Ranch Hollow. — That's kind of creepy. Ranch Hollow.

Val, you ever have any weird stories? Ghost stories? UFO stories? — I just hear a lot of what you say — the same thing, about the old guys from my town. — Oh, really? — Yeah, like they saw somebody, from a specific house or from different

houses, living around there, and they hear noises. — I don't disbelieve it. I won't say I believe it — I don't disbelieve it. — You haven't had any personal experiences? — I've had one ghost experience. — What was that? — But it's so innocuous, it's not even
that interesting. The only thing is, it's interesting because it's a ghost. But my friend and I, we were walking. We'd finished work, and we were rounding the corner to go to the elevator.
And when you round the corner of the building, the elevator is maybe ten, twelve feet away. And it's only two stories, two floors. So as we round the corner, we're about to hit the elevator.
As we get to it, we see someone in the elevator, and the elevator closes before we get in. But it closed right in front of us. So we pressed the button, and then the elevator door opened right away.

And when it opened right away, there was nobody there. And then when I was talking to my friend the next day — we didn't say anything that night — the next day we kind of said, 'Hey, wasn't there someone in the elevator?'
Like, it was impossible for him to have gone into the elevator, for the door to shut, for him to go down and then come back up. Because it was a notoriously slow elevator.
And I said, 'You know what, I didn't look at the whole thing. All I saw was from the pants down. He was wearing brown suit pants.' He goes, 'Yeah, he was wearing a brown suit.'
So that's when we knew we saw the same thing, experienced the same phenomenon. — I got something like that too. When I wasn't sober, I was at a dive bar with two of my homies.
And we're drinking beers. At the end of the night, we met this one dude — I don't want to say his name. He's like, 'Hey, you guys want to come over and party and drink?
I got more beers at my place.' He lived in the Hollywood Hills somewhere. We're like, 'Cool.' Ended up going there. He had a bunch of Pabst Blue Ribbons in the fridge. This dude was a DJ, too.
He had a lot of vinyl, but he wasn't playing normal music. He was playing old Elvis records. And then all of a sudden — it's late now — he's like, 'You guys want to eat mushrooms?'

'I have mushrooms.' So we're like, yeah. He has a Ziploc baggie, and it's like the same way you'd eat potato chips — that's how we were eating these mushrooms. And so, about an hour later, I'm listening.
This is creepy music, I mean, you know. My back is to them, and my friends are both looking out into the living room area. They're facing that way.
And I'm looking at them, squatting down, listening to the music. And they say to the dude that lived there, 'Hey, do you have a roommate here?'
He's like, 'No.' And they both saw a kid come out of one of the rooms, wearing like a rain jacket, a hood, walk out into the bathroom. But there was nobody.
It was just — yeah, he lived by himself. But his response was kind of creepy. He was like, 'Oh yeah, don't mind him.' So he knew this ghost, or whoever it was, was there.

So that was a creepy night. This guy had some cool, interesting music. What about you? — That happened to my little brother. — You saw something? — No, he was — see, everybody had gone to school, so he was staying at the house.
